_readme: Curated names for atomic openings. Everything not listed here is named by
rule in trainer/openings.py, and anything you rename in the UI overrides
both. `line` is the SAN move sequence, space separated; '' is the start.
`source` is the provenance of the NAME, not of the move:
standard    - the name standard chess already gives this exact move order.
community   - a name atomic players actually use.
descriptive - coined here, and saying so rather than pretending otherwise.
First moves borrow their standard-chess names on purpose. 1.Nh3 really is
the Amar Opening whatever variant is being played, the names are already in
everyone's head, and inventing a parallel vocabulary for the one ply atomic
shares with chess would make the index harder to use, not easier. Atomic
diverges from move 1 onwards, and so does the naming.

openings.name: King's Knight Opening
openings.note: 52% of atomic games and the main road. Nf3 eyes e5 and g5, the two squares an undefended Black king's position leaks from.

openings.name: King's Pawn Opening
openings.note: The standard-chess reflex, and it scores 43% here: the e-pawn's chief job in atomic is to be captured next to something that matters.

openings.name: Van 't Kruijs Opening
openings.note: A sideline in chess and a main line in atomic: it opens the diagonals for Qf3/Qh5 and Bd3 without putting a pawn where it can be blasted.

openings.name: Amar Opening
openings.note: A joke in standard chess. Fairy-Stockfish's first choice in atomic, against a field that plays 1.Nf3 seven times as often — the repo's open 1.Nh3-versus-1.Nf3 question is exactly this disagreement.

openings.name: King's Knight Opening: f6 Defence
openings.note: 76% of Black's replies and the position most atomic theory is about. 1...f6 takes e5 and g5 away from the knight and clears f7 for the king, which is the whole defensive idea of the variant.

openings.name: King's Knight Opening: f6 Defence, Kapsarov Attack
openings.note: Both knights out before a pawn moves. Black answers 2...c6 or 2...Nh6; the g4 push against the latter is the sharpest line in the opening.

openings.name: King's Knight Opening: f6 Defence, e3 System
openings.note: The move community theory calls best on both practical and theoretical grounds: it prepares 3.Ne5, which very few of Black's third moves actually stop.

openings.name: King's Knight Opening: f6 Defence, Nd4 System
openings.note: The knight re-routes to f5 or b5 rather than staying on f3 to be traded. Black's 2...Nh6 is the main answer and 3.Nf5 the main test.

openings.name: King's Knight Opening: e5 Counterattack
openings.note: 12% of Black's replies and the only popular one that hits back immediately. 2.Ng5 is the critical try; 2.Nxe5 is not, because the knight dies with the pawn — which is also why this is a counter rather than a gambit.
